```markdown
# SEC filing ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (Proposed; covers O1 only, its §2.2 puts O2–O3 out of scope), specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md (Proposed).
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
Choices made: uv workspace with packages sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest (scaffolds only).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes at 3 req/s; SEC full-index and daily-index directories. Measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for full history at 3 req/s; index row count × request rate, not yet measured |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until the submissions are on disk; no basis yet |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Index table
      Objective: Ingest the real quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: one filing-index table queryable by CIK, form type, filing date and archive path; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: the table holds rows from every quarterly index in the range the stage sets, plus the daily indexes through the run date; the findings file records row count, bytes downloaded, request count and wall time of the real run
      Leaves out: manifests and replay: Stage 4; point-in-time reconciliation: Stage 5; full validation suite: Stage 6; scheduling and deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the submissions that the index table's rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submission files on disk, each locatable from its index row; a list of rows whose download failed
      Exit: for the range the stage sets, every named submission is on disk or listed as failed, with the counts and the measured download rate recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and replay: Stage 4; full validation suite: Stage 6; scheduling and deployment, including one request budget across concurrent collectors: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick out 10-K and 8-K filings from the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submission files and Stage 1's table
      Produces: main documents of 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its index row
      Exit: every 10-K and 8-K submission in Stage 2's range has its main document extracted or is listed with a reason; counts per form are recorded
      Leaves out: manifests and replay: Stage 4; full validation suite: Stage 6; scheduling and deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and replay
      Objective: Record provenance for every downloaded file and reprocess from stored bytes.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (quality: manifests and replay)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest tying each table row, submission and extracted document to its source URL, hash and receipt time
      Exit: every output traces to its source bytes; a reprocess from stored bytes makes zero SEC requests and yields the same table and documents
      Leaves out: point-in-time reconciliation: Stage 5; full validation suite: Stage 6; scheduling and deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and keep corrections without losing earlier versions.
      Outcomes: O1 (quality: point-in-time reconciliation)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest
      Produces: an index table with versioned history of additions, changes and withdrawals
      Exit: a re-read of a changed quarterly index records each addition, change and withdrawal; a reader can read the table as it stood on an earlier date
      Leaves out: full validation suite: Stage 6; scheduling and deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover the pipeline with tests on committed fixtures that make no SEC requests.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (quality: full validation suite)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: a CI suite over the index formats in range, submissions and extraction
      Exit: CI passes on fixtures for every index format in range; HTML error pages, truncated files and malformed rows fail closed; CI makes no SEC requests
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run ingestion unattended on a schedule within one shared SEC request budget.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (quality: scheduling and deployment)
      Consumes: Stage 6's suite passing; Stages 4–5 manifest and reconciliation
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports
      Exit: observed scheduled runs ingest new daily indexes and their submissions; a missed day is caught up; concurrent runs never exceed the configured request rate
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-ingestion-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list: re-run the gap rubric over O1–O3 with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Each unmet outcome exits as a new stage or a conscious deferral with a written why.
```
